L281: Getting Started On this page
L282: # Build a Project from Scratch
L283: 
L284: Copy page
L285: 
L286: Note
L287: 
L288: If you already created a project with the CLI or by cloning an example from the cite56†Getting Started guide, you can skip this guide and move on to the cite63†Routing guide.
L289: 
L290: So you want to build a TanStack Start project from scratch?
L291: 
L292: This guide will help you build a very basic TanStack Start web application. Together, we will use TanStack Start to:
L293: 
L294:   * Serve an index page
L295: 
L296:   * Display a counter
L297: 
L298:   * Increment the counter on the server and client
L299: cite66†Here is what that will look like†stackblitz.com L300: 
L301: Let's create a new project directory and initialize it.
L302: 
L303: shell
L304: 
L305:     mkdir myApp
L306:     cd myApp
L307:     npm init -y
L308: 
L309: Note
L310: 
L311: We use npm in all of these examples, but you can use your package manager of choice instead.
L312: ## TypeScript Configurationcite67†# L313: 
L314: We highly recommend using TypeScript with TanStack Start. Create a tsconfig.json file with at least the following settings:
L315: 
L316: json
L317: 
L318:     {
L319:       "compilerOptions": {
L320:         "jsx": "react-jsx",
L321:         "moduleResolution": "Bundler",
L322:         "module": "ESNext",
L323:         "target": "ES2022",
L324:         "skipLibCheck": true,
L325:         "strictNullChecks": true
L326:       }
L327:     }
L328: 
L329: Note
L330: Enabling verbatimModuleSyntax can result in server bundles leaking into client bundles. It is recommended to keep this option disabled.
L331: ## Install Dependenciescite68†# L332: 
L333: TanStack Start is powered by cite5†TanStack Router and supports cite69†Vite†vite.dev or cite70†Rsbuild†rsbuild.dev as the build tool.
L334: 
L335: To install Start and Router, run:
L336: 
L337: shell
L338: 
L339:     npm i @tanstack/react-start @tanstack/react-router
L340: 
L341: You'll also need React:
L342: 
L343: shell
L344: 
L345:     npm i react react-dom
L346: 
L347: Install the build tool and React integration you want to use:
L348: 
L349: Vite Rsbuild
L350: 
L351: shell
L352: 
L353:     npm i -D vite @vitejs/plugin-react
L354: 
L355: shell
L356: 
L357:     npm i -D @rsbuild/core @rsbuild/plugin-react
L358: If you use Vite, you can also use @vitejs/plugin-react-swc instead of @vitejs/plugin-react.
L359: 
L360: and some TypeScript:
L361: 
L362: shell
L363: 
L364:     npm i -D typescript @types/react @types/react-dom @types/node
L365: ## Update Configuration Filescite71†# L366: 
L367: We'll then update our package.json to use your build tool's CLI and set "type": "module":
L368: 
L369: Vite Rsbuild
L370: 
L371: json
L372: 
L373:     {
L374:       // ...
L375:       "type": "module",
L376:       "scripts": {
L377:         "dev": "vite dev",
L378:         "build": "vite build"
L379:       }
L380:     }
L381: 
L382: json
L383: 
L384:     {
L385:       // ...
L386:       "type": "module",
L387:       "scripts": {
L388:         "dev": "rsbuild dev",
L389:         "build": "rsbuild build"
L390:       }
L391:     }
L392: 
L393: Then configure TanStack Start's build tool plugin:
L394: 
L395: Vite Rsbuild
L396: vite.config.ts
L397: 
L398:     import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
L399:     import { tanstackStart } from '@tanstack/react-start/plugin/vite'
L400:     import viteReact from '@vitejs/plugin-react'
L401: 
L402:     export default defineConfig({
L403:       server: {
L404:         port: 3000,
L405:       },
L406:       resolve: {
L407:         tsconfigPaths: true,
L408:       },
L409:       plugins: [
L410:         tanstackStart(),
L411:         // react's vite plugin must come after start's vite plugin
L412:         viteReact(),
L413:       ],
L414:     })
L415: 
L416: rsbuild.config.ts
L417:     import { defineConfig } from '@rsbuild/core'
L418:     import { pluginReact } from '@rsbuild/plugin-react'
L419:     import { tanstackStart } from '@tanstack/react-start/plugin/rsbuild'
L420: 
L421:     export default defineConfig({
L422:       server: {
L423:         port: 3000,
L424:       },
L425:       plugins: [pluginReact(), tanstackStart()],
L426:     })
L427: ## Add the Basic Templatingcite72†# L428: 
L429: There are 2 required files for TanStack Start usage:
L430: 
L431:   1. The router configuration
L432: 
L433:   2. The root of your application
L434: 
L435: Once configuration is done, we'll have a file tree that looks like the following:
L436: 
L437: plaintext
L438: 
L439:     .
L440:     ├── src/
L441:     │   ├── routes/
L442:     │   │   └── `__root.tsx`
L443:     │   ├── `router.tsx`
L444:     │   ├── `routeTree.gen.ts`
L445:     ├── `vite.config.ts` or `rsbuild.config.ts`
L446:     ├── `package.json`
L447:     └── `tsconfig.json`
L448: ## The Router Configurationcite73†# L449: 
L450: This is the file that will dictate the behavior of TanStack Router used within Start. Here, you can configure everything from the default cite74†preloading functionality to cite75†caching staleness .
L451: 
L452: Note
L453: 
L454: You won't have a routeTree.gen.ts file yet. This file will be generated when you run TanStack Start for the first time.
L455: 
L456: tsx
L457: 
L458:     // src/router.tsx
L459:     import { createRouter } from '@tanstack/react-router'
L460:     import { routeTree } from './routeTree.gen'
L461:     export function getRouter() {
L462:       const router = createRouter({
L463:         routeTree,
L464:         scrollRestoration: true,
L465:       })
L466: 
L467:       return router
L468:     }
L469: ## The Root of Your Applicationcite76†# L470: 
L471: Finally, we need to create the root of our application. This is the entry point for all other routes. The code in this file will wrap all other routes in the application.
L472: 
L473: tsx
L474: 
L475:     // src/routes/__root.tsx
L476:     import type { ReactNode } from 'react'
L477:     import {
L478:       Outlet,
L479:       createRootRoute,
L480:       HeadContent,
L481:       Scripts,
L482:     } from '@tanstack/react-router'
L483:     export const Route = createRootRoute({
L484:       head: () => ({
L485:         meta: [
L486:           {
L487:             charSet: 'utf-8',
L488:           },
L489:           {
L490:             name: 'viewport',
L491:             content: 'width=device-width, initial-scale=1',
L492:           },
L493:           {
L494:             title: 'TanStack Start Starter',
L495:           },
L496:         ],
L497:       }),
L498:       component: RootComponent,
L499:     })
L500: 
L501:     function RootComponent() {
L502:       return (
L503:         <RootDocument>
L504:           <Outlet />
L505:         </RootDocument>
L506:       )
L507:     }
L508:     function RootDocument({ children }: Readonly<{ children: ReactNode }>) {
L509:       return (
L510:         <html>
L511:           <head>
L512:             <HeadContent />
L513:           </head>
L514:           <body>
L515:             {children}
L516:             <Scripts />
L517:           </body>
L518:         </html>
L519:       )
L520:     }
L521: ## Writing Your First Routecite77†# L522: 
L523: Now that we have the basic templating setup, we can write our first route. This is done by creating a new file in the src/routes directory.
L524: 
L525: tsx
L526: 
L527:     // src/routes/index.tsx
L528:     import * as fs from 'node:fs'
L529:     import { createFileRoute, useRouter } from '@tanstack/react-router'
L530:     import { createServerFn } from '@tanstack/react-start'
L531: 
L532:     const filePath = 'count.txt'
L533:     async function readCount() {
L534:       return parseInt(
L535:         await fs.promises.readFile(filePath, 'utf-8').catch(() => '0'),
L536:       )
L537:     }
L538: 
L539:     const getCount = createServerFn({
L540:       method: 'GET',
L541:     }).handler(() => {
L542:       return readCount()
L543:     })
L544: 
L545:     const updateCount = createServerFn({ method: 'POST' })
L546:       .validator((d: number) => d)
L547:       .handler(async ({ data }) => {
L548:         const count = await readCount()
L549:         await fs.promises.writeFile(filePath, `${count + data}`)
L550:       })
L551:     export const Route = createFileRoute('/')({
L552:       component: Home,
L553:       loader: async () => await getCount(),
L554:     })
L555: 
L556:     function Home() {
L557:       const router = useRouter()
L558:       const state = Route.useLoaderData()
L559: 
L560:       return (
L561:         <button
L562:           type="button"
L563:           onClick={() => {
L564:             updateCount({ data: 1 }).then(() => {
L565:               router.invalidate()
L566:             })
L567:           }}
L568:         >
L569:           Add 1 to {state}?
L570:         </button>
L571:       )
L572:     }
L573: That's it! You've now set up a TanStack Start project and written your first route.
L574: 
L575: You can now run npm run dev to start your server and navigate to http://localhost:3000 to see your route in action.
L576: 
L577: You want to deploy your application? Check out the cite78†hosting guide .
